questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's population policy:
1. India was the first country to launch a national family planning programme (1952)
2. India's TFR has fallen below replacement level (2.1) as per NFHS-5
3. India will surpass China as the most populous country
4. National Population Policy 2000 set a target of achieving TFR of 2.1 by 2010
questions.explanation: All correct. India's family planning (1952): world's first national programme. NFHS-5 (2021): TFR 2.0 (below 2.1 replacement). India surpassed China in population (2023, UN estimates). NPP 2000: target TFR 2.1 by 2010 — missed by over a decade (achieved ~2021). Challenge now: demographic TRANSITION — southern states aging, northern states still growing. Kerala TFR: 1.8; Bihar: 3.0. This north-south divide has political implications (delimitation debate).

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's Mental Health framework:
1. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 decriminalized attempted suicide
2. It provides the right to access mental healthcare
3. India has approximately 1 psychiatrist per 1 lakh population
4. District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) covers all 780 districts
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — DMHP does NOT cover all 780 districts. It was operational in only ~700+ districts by 2024 (expanded gradually from 27 districts in 1996). Coverage and quality remain uneven — many districts have the programme only on paper with inadequate staff. India's mental health crisis: 150 million+ need treatment, only 30 million access it. The Act (2017) also established Mental Health Review Boards and Advanced Directives for treatment preferences.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's education indicators:
1. India's literacy rate is approximately 77.7% (Census 2011, likely 80%+ now)
2. Female literacy (65.5%) significantly lags male literacy (82.1%)
3. Kerala has the highest literacy rate among states (~96%)
4. RTE Act guarantees free education up to Class 12
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — RTE Act 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education only up to Class 8 (ages 6-14, elementary education), NOT Class 12. For secondary/senior secondary, there's no fundamental right guarantee yet (though government schemes provide support). Gender gap in literacy: ~17 percentage points (improving but persistent). Bihar has lowest literacy (~62%). NEP 2020 aims for 100% youth/adult literacy by 2030.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's healthcare challenges:
1. India's doctor-to-population ratio is approximately 1:834 (WHO recommends 1:1000)
2. Out-of-pocket expenditure pushes ~5 crore people into poverty annually
3. India has a significant rural-urban healthcare divide
4. India has achieved Universal Health Coverage for all citizens
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India has NOT achieved Universal Health Coverage. Despite Ayushman Bharat/PM-JAY (covering 50 crore beneficiaries), significant gaps remain: no OPD coverage, limited secondary care in rural areas, high OOP expenditure (~40%), shortage of specialists, poor primary healthcare infrastructure. UHC means ALL people receive quality services without financial hardship — India is far from this. National Health Policy 2017 targets UHC but path is long.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's Scheduled Castes and affirmative action:
1. SCs constitute approximately 16.6% of India's population (Census 2011)
2. Reservation is provided in education, employment, and legislature (Articles 15, 16, 330, 332)
3. SC sub-categorization for reservation was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2024
4. Creamy layer concept applies to SC/ST reservations just like OBC
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — creamy layer concept traditionally did NOT apply to SC/ST reservations (only OBC). Indra Sawhney (1992) explicitly excluded SC/ST from creamy layer. However, the 2024 SC judgment on sub-categorization opened debate about applying creamy layer within SC/ST (for prioritizing more backward among SCs). This is evolving and politically sensitive. SCs: 16.6% (201 million), reservation in services capped at proportion of population.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's elderly population and welfare:
1. India's 60+ population is approximately 10.5% (Census 2011, likely 12%+ now)
2. Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 mandates children to support parents
3. National Policy on Older Persons was announced in 1999
4. India has a comprehensive universal pension system covering all elderly
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India does NOT have a comprehensive universal pension. IGNOAPS (Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme) provides only ₹200-500/month to BPL elderly (grossly inadequate). NPS is for organized sector. Majority of elderly (especially in informal sector) have no pension. The Act (2007) allows elderly to claim maintenance from children through Tribunals, and provides for old age homes. Aging challenge: by 2050, India will have 300+ million elderly — social security infrastructure is unprepared.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's disability rights:
1. Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 replaced the 1995 Act
2. It recognizes 21 types of disabilities (up from 7 in the 1995 Act)
3. It mandates 5% reservation in higher education and 4% in government jobs
4. India has ratified the UN Convention on Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD)
questions.explanation: All correct. RPwD Act 2016: comprehensive law (replaced PwD Act 1995). 21 disabilities recognized (including acid attack victims, thalassemia, hemophilia, sickle cell, autism, learning disabilities, cerebral palsy). Reservation: 5% in higher education, 4% in government employment. India ratified UNCRPD in 2007. Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyaan): making public spaces, transport, ICT accessible. Challenge: 2.68 crore PwDs (Census 2011, likely undercount), most face barriers in employment, education, mobility.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's drug abuse problem:
1. NDPS Act, 1985 is the primary legislation against drug trafficking
2. The Act differentiates between small, commercial, and intermediate quantities
3. National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) focuses on prevention and rehabilitation
4. Cannabis is completely legal in all parts of India
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — cannabis/marijuana is NOT legal in India. NDPS Act prohibits cultivation, production, sale of cannabis. However, 'bhang' (made from leaves, not flowering buds) has some legal grey area in certain states (used in Holi). Punjab drug crisis (chitta/heroin), NE India (opium belt), and synthetic drugs are major concerns. NAPDDR (2018-2025): awareness, treatment, rehabilitation. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (2020): 272 vulnerable districts identified for focused intervention.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about Manual Scavenging in India:
1. Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 bans the practice
2. Despite the ban, manual scavenging deaths continue to be reported
3. NAMASTE scheme replaces Swacchta Abhiyan for mechanization of sewer cleaning
4. Safai Karamchari Andolan (SKA) has been instrumental in fighting for abolition
questions.explanation: All correct. MS Act 2013: bans employment of manual scavengers, punishes employers (₹5 lakh fine/5 years imprisonment). Despite ban: 300+ deaths/year in sewer/septic tank cleaning (mostly Dalits). NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem, 2023): replaces SRMS scheme, aims for zero fatalities through mechanization, PPE provision, health insurance for sanitation workers. SKA (Bezwada Wilson, Magsaysay Award 2016): major advocacy role. SC has repeatedly issued directions for compensation and rehabilitation.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to Gender Budgeting in India:
1. Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB) was introduced in India's budget from 2005-06
2. It has two parts: Part A (100% women-specific schemes) and Part B (at least 30% for women)
3. A Gender Budget Cell exists in all ministries
4. India's female labour force participation rate (FLFPR) has been historically low (~25-30%)
questions.explanation: All correct. GRB (2005-06 onwards): Government tracks gender-specific allocations in budget. Part A: schemes with 100% allocation for women (Beti Bachao, One Stop Centres). Part B: schemes with >30% women component (MGNREGA, PMAY). Gender Budget Cells: in 57 ministries/departments (per guidelines). FLFPR: India among lowest globally (~25-30% by NSSO, though PLFS 2022-23 shows improvement to 37% with rural women's farm participation counted). Gender gaps persist in wages, ownership, representation.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's migration patterns:
1. Inter-state migration in India is approximately 9 crore (Census 2011)
2. Marriage is the primary reason for female migration in India
3. Migrant workers faced severe hardship during COVID-19 lockdown (2020)
4. e-Shram portal was launched to register unorganized sector workers
questions.explanation: All correct. Census 2011: 45.6 crore migrants (total, including intra-district); inter-state: ~9 crore. Female migration: 70%+ for marriage (reflecting social norms, not economic migration). COVID crisis (March 2020): millions of migrant workers stranded, walked hundreds of km home — exposed lack of social security portability. e-Shram (2021): registered 30 crore+ unorganized workers (construction, domestic, gig, street vendors). One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) addresses food security portability for migrants.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to India's Juvenile Justice system:
1. Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 replaced the 2000 Act
2. It allows 16-18 year olds accused of heinous crimes to be tried as adults
3. This provision was added after the Nirbhaya case (2012)
4. Child Care Institutions (CCIs) are the only permitted form of care under the Act
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — the Act promotes FAMILY-BASED care (foster care, sponsorship, adoption) over institutional care (CCIs). Institutionalization is meant to be a LAST resort. JJ Act 2015: after Nirbhaya case (one accused was 17, couldn't be tried as adult under 2000 Act — public outrage). Now: Juvenile Justice Board assesses mental capacity of 16-18 accused in heinous crimes; if mature, can be tried by Children's Court. Also strengthened adoption framework (Central Adoption Resource Authority/CARA).
